title: Bounded ordinary constant-field realization of field-stage complexes
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and a scheme $Y$. Use a small representative of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant ring sheaves $R_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and their ordinary derived categories. For each finite coefficient field $E\subset\Qlb$, let $R_E=\mathcal O_E$, with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and put $B_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The compatible maps from the constant sheaf $(R_E)_Y$ to its constant quotient sheaves give a ring-sheaf map $u_E:(R_E)_Y\to B_E$. Let $U_E:D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_E))\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R_E)$ be termwise restriction of scalars along $u_E$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

There are functors
$$J_E:D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E)$$
from the raw scalar localizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], specified on the integral objects $C\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] by
$$J_E(C)=U_E(C)\otimes^L_{(R_E)_Y}E_Y,$$
using ordinary derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor], and on a scalar-localized morphism $f\otimes a$, $a\in E$, by $J_E(f\otimes a)=a\,J_E(f)$. These formulas give well-defined $E$-linear functors, and every $J_E(C)$ is cohomologically bounded [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

For each inclusion $E\subset L$ of finite coefficient fields there is a natural isomorphism
$$J_L(C\otimes_E L)\cong J_E(C)\otimes^L_{E_Y}L_Y,$$
where $C\otimes_E L$ is the transition functor of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The isomorphisms are compatible with identity inclusions and with composition for $E\subset L\subset M$. Consequently the formulas
$$J_{\Qlb}(E,C)=J_E(C)\otimes^L_{E_Y}(\Qlb)_Y$$
and, for a morphism represented over a common finite field $L$, its image under $J_L$ followed by scalar extension to $(\Qlb)_Y$, give a well-defined $\Qlb$-linear functor
$$J_{\Qlb}:D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)\longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Qlb)$$
from the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Its values are cohomologically bounded. All coefficient sheaves in the targets of $J_E$ and $J_{\Qlb}$ are the discrete constant sheaves; no assertion that these target objects have constructible cohomology as constant-coefficient sheaves is made.

external.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), pp. 61–62; rationalization and finite-coefficient-field descent, followed here by restriction to constant coefficients

proof.text: For a finite field stage E and an integral representative C in D^b_c(Y, O_E), the coefficient maps (O_E)_Y -> B_E define U_E by restriction of scalars. Restriction leaves the underlying sheaf of abelian groups and therefore preserves kernels, cokernels, quasi-isomorphisms, and distinguished triangles; termwise restriction consequently gives a triangulated functor D(Mod(B_E)) -> D(Y_proet, O_E). The constant sheaf (O_E)_Y is the coefficient ring used by the ordinary derived tensor, so U_E(C) tensor^L_{(O_E)_Y} E_Y is an object of D(Y_proet,E).

source.place: first sentence: realization by restriction to the constant integral ring and inversion of the uniformizer

proof.text: The integral derived tensor is functorial and independent of the K-flat resolution, so C maps to U_E(C) tensor^L_{(O_E)_Y} E_Y and an integral morphism f maps to the corresponding derived-tensor morphism. The integral derived category is O_E-linear, and the derived category construction preserves that scalar action; hence this assignment sends af to a times its image. By the Hom formula defining the raw scalar localization, the O_E-linear assignment extends uniquely on morphisms by J_E(f tensor a)=a J_E(f), and it respects identities, composition, shifts, and distinguished triangles. Thus it is a well-defined E-linear functor J_E on D^b_c(Y,E).

source.place: first sentence: realization by restriction and inversion, together with the scalar-localized morphism formula

proof.text: Let C be integral and choose an interval [r,s] supplied by the uniform bound in the definition of D^b_c(Y,O_E) for all reductions C tensor^L_{O_E} A_{E,n}. Let V be an affine open of Y; it is an object of Y_proet and V_proet is the localized site Y_proet/V, so restriction to V is exact, preserves countable products, constant sheaves and their inverse limit B_E, and commutes with the derived reductions (computed termwise on a K-flat representative, which stays K-flat after restriction). Hence C|_V is derived complete for its quotient tower (the Roos triangle of the definition restricts to a distinguished triangle), and its reduction at n=1, C|_V tensor^L k_V with k=A_{E,1} the residue field, has cohomology only in [r,s]. Every sheaf N of k_W-modules (W an object over V) is flat: the tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product over the field k, which is exact. So (C|_V tensor^L k_V)|_W tensor^L N is computed termwise and has cohomology sheaves H^j tensor_k N, which vanish for j outside [r,s]; that reduction has Tor amplitude in [r,s]. The completed residue-cohomology bound (Tag 09C2 (1)) applied on the quasi-compact affine V gives H^i(C|_V)=0 outside [r,s]. The affine opens of Y cover the final object of Y_proet and H^i(C)|_V=H^i(C|_V), so H^i(C)=0 outside [r,s]. Restriction of scalars does not change the underlying cohomology sheaf, and E_Y is a flat (O_E)_Y-module (the filtered colimit of the free modules varpi_E^{-m}(O_E)_Y); therefore J_E(C)=U_E(C) tensor^L E_Y has cohomology H^i(C) tensor E_Y and the same vanishing interval. This proves cohomological boundedness, with the bound chosen before any test sheaf.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, assertion (1) and proof; the affine-local application is the same completeness and residue-Tor argument

proof.text: For E subset L write R=B_E and S=B_L. The finite-free completed scalar comparison identifies the derived change of rings C tensor^L_R S with the strict-tower integral scalar extension C tensor_{O_E} O_L, naturally in C (C is derived complete). Choose an O_E-basis e_1,...,e_d of O_L. Since varpi_E^n O_L = varpi_L^{ne} O_L, the towers (O_L/varpi_L^m)_Y and (O_L/varpi_E^n O_L)_Y = (A_{E,n})_Y^{d} are cofinal, and constant sheaves and limits commute with finite sums; so the map R tensor_{(O_E)_Y} (O_L)_Y -> S is an isomorphism of R-algebras. For a K-flat resolution P -> C over R, C tensor^L_R S is P tensor_R S, and termwise U_L(P tensor_R S) = U_E(P) tensor_{(O_E)_Y} (O_L)_Y as (O_L)_Y-modules. Since (O_L)_Y is free over (O_E)_Y and L_Y is a flat (O_L)_Y-module, derived tensors with them are computed termwise, and the associator gives U_L(C tensor^L_R S) tensor^L_{(O_L)_Y} L_Y = U_E(P) tensor_{(O_E)_Y} L_Y = (U_E(C) tensor^L_{(O_E)_Y} E_Y) tensor^L_{E_Y} L_Y. This isomorphism is natural in integral morphisms by functoriality of the derived tensor, independent of P by resolution independence, and O_E-linear, hence natural for scalar-localized morphisms f tensor a. The integral scalar extension lies in D^b_c(Y,O_L), and the raw localization D^b_c(Y,L) has the same objects, so this integral object is C tensor_E L itself; we obtain the natural isomorphism J_L(C tensor_E L) isomorphic to J_E(C) tensor^L_{E_Y} L_Y.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), pp. 61–62, with the finite-free completed comparison and ordinary constant-coefficient restriction

proof.text: The comparison in the preceding step is the identity for E=L and is compatible with a tower E subset L subset M, because both sides are obtained from the same iterated derived tensor and the finite-free completion comparison is natural. The scalar-extension composition isomorphism (C tensor_E L) tensor_L M isomorphic to C tensor_E M gives the corresponding associativity square for the J-comparisons. For an object of the common-stage category D^b_c(Y,Qbar), choose a finite field E and a representative C, and define J_Qbar(E,C)=J_E(C) tensor^L_{E_Y} (Qbar)_Y. Every morphism is represented over one finite common field; applying J at that field and then extending scalars gives a map. Enlarging the common field changes it by the compatible comparison just proved, while the common-stage composition law makes successive enlargements agree. Hence the formula is independent of representatives and defines a Qbar-linear functor. The boundedness of its values follows from the finite-stage bound and flat scalar extension, and all target coefficient sheaves are discrete constant sheaves by construction.
